articles.title: The Moza R5 Racing Wheel Offers 5.5Nm of Direct Drive Force Feedback for an Affordable Price
articles.summary: If you're a big fan of racing games, you've probably already got yourself a wheel. But if you're still rocking an entry level gear- or belt-driven wheel because you've been held back by the steep cost of direct drive, then check out this new deal.
body: The R5 is not Moza's least expensive direct drive wheel. That honor goes to the Moza R3, which retails for $279.99 and is not currently on sale. The primary difference between the two is maximum torque: the R5 offers 5.5Nm of force compared to 3.9Nm from the R3. Both are less expensive than other alternatives: Logitech's G RS50 is $600 (for the wheel only), Fanatec's CSL DD Ready2Race Bundle is $540, Simagic's Green Flag Bundle is $600, and Thrustmaster's T598 is $466. Some do offer advantages like a higher torque ceiling or console compatibility, but if value is king it's hard to beat Moza.

So what makes direct drive the gold standard for racing sims? Direct drive wheels connect directly to the motor, which translates to immediate force feedback with zero latency and no lost power delivery from gear or belt-drive resistance. The higher the torque rating, the wider range of sensitivity. The Moza R5 is a big step up in immersion compared to a gear or belt driven wheel, and 5Nm is considered the baseline for bringing out the best of what direct drive has to offer.
points: If you're a big fan of racing games, you've probably already got yourself a wheel.
But if you're still rocking an entry level gear- or belt-driven wheel because you've been held back by the steep cost of direct drive, then check out this new deal.

articles.title: Resident Evil Requiem Producer “Explains” Game’s Title, Confusing Us More
articles.summary: The meaning of Resident Evil Requiem's title appeared to be self-evident when it was released earlier this year. However, Resident Evil producer Jun Takeuchi's explanation for the title from the recently published Biohazard 30th Anniversary Special may be a head-scratcher for even the series'…
body: "'Requiem' isn't just a title chosen for its meaning of 'requiem,'" said Takeuchi via GamesRadar. "The spelling of Requiem (REQUIEM) contains not only the 'RE (response)'... but also a 'Q (question).' In other words, this 'Requiem' presents both an 'answer' and a 'question.' I will explain the meaning of that at some point in the future."
More intriguingly, Takeuchi indicated that the Resident Evil remake games and the current titles have been building towards a crossover since Resident Evil Village.

"Currently, Resident Evil operates on a two-pronged approach: The numbered titles allow players to experience the ongoing drama of the series, while the remake series lets them experience the past," added Takeuchi. "Eventually, the remake series will catch up to the era of the numbered titles, and the mechanisms for that are already being considered. In fact, preparations for this have been gradually underway since Resident Evil Village, including the appearance of names like Umbrella and Spencer, and the reappearance of Raccoon City in Requiem. This is all in preparation for a crossover."
points: The meaning of Resident Evil Requiem's title appeared to be self-evident when it was released earlier this year.

articles.summary: Rockstar has suggested that GTA 6 probably won't feature some key Florida attractions, such as Disney World and SeaWorld. As part of a recent Game Informer cover story on GTA 6, Rockstar Games seemed to suggest that its fictionalized version of Florida, known as Leonida, won't include every iconic…
body: "We have to constantly evaluate the diversity of landscapes, towns, structures, landmarks, vistas, plant species, rock formations and everything else before we work with design and narrative to distill a list down that best works with and serves the game’s needs," he said. "So, while we may not have those exact locations, everything we have is geared to getting that full Florida experience!”

Rockstar didn't rule out any specific locations, but the comment does suggest that you won't find every major attraction in GTA 6. GTA 5 allowed players to explore the Venice Beach Boardwalk, which featured the pier and its various activities. Players could ride a rollercoaster and a ferris wheel, but generally speaking, it wasn't anything to write home about. There's no reason to do it more than once, and as a result, building an entire park around something like that may not be the best use of development resources.

articles.title: The Splinter Cell Remake Is Still Lurking In The Shadows
articles.summary: A remake of the original Splinter Cell game was first announced nearly five years ago, and since then, we've seen exactly zero seconds of the game in action, or even a trailer.
body: Spotted by Insider Gaming, job openings for a few different positions, including level designer and producer, have been posted within the last few months. This isn't necessarily indicative of how far along the project is--people are hired and leave all the time--but it does at least let us know that the project is still in active development. It's also not the first time we've seen job listings pop up, but with company in as volatile a state as Ubisoft, you never know.

It's unclear exactly what shape this remake will take, as geopolitical dynamics have changed quite a bit since 2002. It's also unclear how much influence it would take from the later games in the series, with Conviction and Blacklist both including more action-aligned mechanics like Mark & Execute.

Since the release of Splinter Cell Blacklist in 2013, we haven't gotten a new Splinter Cell game. Sam Fisher has made numerous appearances, however, including a few guest missions in Ghost Recon and an inclusion in Rainbow Six Siege. The Netflix animated series also released last year, with Liev Schreiber taking over voice duties from Michael Ironside.

articles.title: Xbox CEO Insists It’s Not For Sale Amid Studio Closures, Layoffs
articles.summary: The " Xbox reset " has people wondering whether Microsoft is preparing to exit the video game business, but Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has flatly denied that the gaming division will be put up for sale. "Xbox is not for sale," Sharma said to The New York Times.
body: Sharma's comments come in the wake of analysts predicting that Microsoft could sell Xbox off entirely. Compared with Microsoft's profitable cloud computing and artificial intelligence businesses, Xbox has paled in comparison, and the gamble on Xbox Game Pass hasn't paid off, despite Microsoft investing tens of billions in acquiring several video game publishers and studios over the years. Xbox’s accountability margins amount to only a 3% profit, a small return on investment for its parent company.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has said that Xbox will have to start pulling its weight under Sharma's leadership, and the Xbox CEO previously told employees that the Xbox business was not in a healthy state. Nadella has also praised Sharma's cuts at Xbox, saying they have led to a "streamlining" of the division.

articles.title: You Can Hate The Sonic Movies, But They Help The Games Get Made, Sega Says
articles.summary: Sonic has had a rough go at things lately, what with the myriad games that haven't been hitting like they used to. Sega appears to be aware of that and has acknowledged that, although the games have struggled recently, the franchise as a whole is back in the zeitgeist again--and it's all thanks to…
body: In an interview with Automaton at the Tokyo Game Show, series producer Takashi Iizuka spoke about the impact that director Jeff Fowler's three live-action movies have had on repopularizing Sonic again.

"Thanks to the movies, awareness of the Sonic series has grown, and more people around the world have become interested in Sonic as a character and in the games," Iizuka said when asked about the positive effect other media has had on the franchise. "That has contributed to game sales as well. Strong game sales mean we have more resources available when making the next title, which allows us to deliver something of even higher quality. That creates a positive cycle. In that sense, multimedia and transmedia expansion are majorly beneficial for the games."

Iizuka went on to say that movies weren't the only medium that has improved Sonic the Hedgehog's cachet in recent times. Anime has contributed as well, and so has Netflix, which has made film and television production more ubiquitous for Sega.

articles.title: Ace Combat 8’s Stellar Multiplayer Reveals the Terrors of Live-Service Games
articles.summary: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is one of the best games I’ve played this year. Its 25-hour single-player campaign, featuring 30 thrilling missions, is worth the price of admission alone.
body: Due to the nature of online servers, I wasn’t able to play much Ace Combat Online ahead of Ace Combat 8 ’s review embargo. I only had access to the mode for a few hours, where I moved through a blitz of rotating playlists with press and creators, rather than the wider player population who’s playing now — not substantial enough to pass much judgment. Now that Ace Combat Online is live (at least for the diehards who preordered the base game), I have a much better feel for its multiplayer, and it comes with some real highs and lows. The moment-to-moment action is tense and exciting, but you’ll need to wade through a lot of menus and live-service headaches to appreciate it.

When you first pop into Ace Combat Online, the experience can be immediately overwhelming. After creating a character, you’re dropped into a Destiny-like social hub lined with other players and vendors. Loading into a mission, checking challenges, editing planes, buying new gear, managing your squad — everything is split between various NPCs. It takes a bit of time to figure out where every feature you need lives.
points: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is one of the best games I’ve played this year.

articles.title: Nintendo Isn't Afraid to Get Political with Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave
articles.summary: When you think about Nintendo, the first thing that comes to mind likely isn't adroit political commentary. It's not something the company frequently, or really ever, engages in. Even Monolith Soft's famously big-picture Xenoblade games tend toward philosophy more than politics.
body: That last line is an eternal truth, but Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, the latest game in the series, released Sept. 17 for Switch 2, takes it very seriously. The entire game is a commentary on nationalism and the dangers of failing to confront the truths of the past, no matter how horrific they may be.
Spoilers ahead for Act 2 and beyond of Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave.

Dagda's story is the same as that of any empire throughout history. Centuries of warfare and conquest expanded its borders, giving rise to a fervent belief in the divinity of that conquest. When the nation's ruler is a god and the offspring of the world's ultimate deity, common folk can be pretty easily convinced. Dagda justifies his latest war in Part 2 by reminding his court (the ones he hasn't killed, anyway) that Sothis, his mother and the progenitor god, tasked him with bringing the continent under his control.

articles.title: Former Halo lead suggests three ways Activision could revive the legendary series, and urges the company to hire laid off Bungie staff
articles.summary: Halo's ex-franchise director, Frank O'Connor, has given Activision a few pointers now that it's in charge of making the next Halo game with a "purpose-built team." Top of the list, hire some devs who were laid off from Bungie and Halo Studios.
body: O'Connor's time with the iconic sci-fi series stretches back to the early 2000s, when he jumped aboard at Bungie and eventually became the series' development director at 343 Industries. He left the studio during an internal shakeup in 2023, shortly before 343 rebranded into Halo Studios, which has since been gutted due to Xbox's "reset."
"There are three paths," O'Connor recently commented on a LinkedIn post, talking about whatever Activision's Halo plans are. "None of these are easy, guaranteed or necessarily viable."

His first suggestion is that Activision could make a "classic" Halo game with the series' familiar, heavy movement and chaotic sandbox "tailored to a core audience [and] scaled" to also be "attractive to a broader one so it can grow (not to mention [the] obvious fact that Halo MP is better [with] more people playing, by mathematical default)."
points: Halo's ex-franchise director, Frank O'Connor, has given Activision a few pointers now that it's in charge of making the next Halo game with a "purpose-built team.

articles.title: 10 Biggest GTA 6 Questions the Previews Haven't Answered Yet
articles.summary: Since Netflix's extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6 debuted back in August, we've heard fairly little from Rockstar Games about 2026's most anticipated video game. That all changed on Sept. 29, when Game Informer shared its 14-page deep dive into GTA 6.
body: While there is surely more information to come in weeks heading up to the Nov. 19 launch, there are plenty of big questions about GTA 6 that we still have no concrete answers for. Here are a few that stand out.

Forgive the inside baseball here, but literally every games journalist on earth right now is wondering if and when Rockstar will share advanced review copies of GTA 6. Sometimes, for very long games, publishers will share copies a month or more in advance. Occasionally, publishers will send out code on Friday evening for a Monday morning embargo. There's no one way of doing it. And Rockstar is an unusual company, and GTA 6 is an unusual game, so even those nebulous rules may not necessarily apply.

What's more, Rockstar has been unusually secretive and selective in its marketing campaign, granting preview access to conventional gaming outlets (IGN, Game Informer) and more mainstream or niche outlets (The New York Times, Dazed) in equal measure. The studio also shared preview footage with a number of YouTube and Twitch content creators ahead of the Netflix showcase in August.

articles.title: "Xbox is not for sale": CEO Asha Sharma says "we will do whatever it takes" to turn the console maker's fortunes around
articles.summary: Despite mass layoffs at multiple first-party studios and major internal shakeups, CEO Asha Sharma has shot down speculation about a potential Xbox buyout.
body: This year, Xbox began a corporate "reset" that plans to cut a total of 3,200 jobs across the company before next summer. So far, the restructure has resulted in three studios going independent (Double Fine, Compulsion Games, Undead Labs), while the fate of Hellblade maker Ninja Theory and Dishonored studio Arkane remains up in the air.

In another dramatic turn earlier this month, Xbox handed Activision the keys to the entire Halo series. Rare and World's Edge (of Age of Empires fame) also moved under the Call of Duty publisher, while Obsidian Entertainment got slotted into Bethesda. That leaves only a handful of developers under the Xbox Game Studios umbrella - The Coalition (Gears of War), Playground Games (Fable, Forza), Mojang (Minecraft), InXile Entertainment (Clockwork Revolution) and what's left of Halo Studios.

To many, this looked like an attempt at streamlining the business to make it more attractive for potential buyers. (Microsoft might have struggled to sell Rare by itself, for example, but that becomes a much easier task when it's bundled in with the company in control of Call of Duty.) A sale isn't on the table at all, however, according to Sharma.
points: Despite mass layoffs at multiple first-party studios and major internal shakeups, CEO Asha Sharma has shot down speculation about a potential Xbox buyout.

articles.title: World of Warcraft: Forever survey pitches new classes to players, including Bard, Witch, and more
articles.summary: The blue elves might not be the only wholly original addition to World of Warcraft: Forever. Blizzard started surveying players about a list of new classes, some of which have been requested by fans for years.
body: Last week, a survey popped up on Blizzard's Battle.net launcher to gauge interest in future additions to WoW: Forever. Participants were told not to publicly share anything from the surveys, but, well, you know how well people listen to warnings on the internet.

The full survey was posted online by some brave soul, and in it you can see several proposed classes: Monk, Demon Hunter, Tinker, Illusionist, San'layn, Necromancer, Rune Knight, Bard, Warden, Witch and Death Knight. Each one has a short description, their role in a group, the kind of gear they'd wear, and a breakdown of some example abilities.

The Witch class, for example, is a ranged damage-dealer and support that wears cloth armor. A cauldron ability that buffs anyone who drinks from it as well as a ranged attack called "Voidbolt" that drains the caster's own life are two of their example abilities.

Bard and Tinker are two classes I always see come up whenever anyone talks about potential new classes. Blizzard's suggested version of them sounds like they'd fit right in with the rest of the roster. The Tinker description says they'd climb into their own mech to fight; Bards would perform songs to heal and buff their allies.
points: The blue elves might not be the only wholly original addition to World of Warcraft: Forever.

body: Out of the shadows comes the newest Support Hero, Doctrine, who can manipulate life itself to heal allies and damage enemies with the help of his Eternal Scepter. Dodge incoming fire with his Shrouded Momentum ability, and send out Invigorating Drones to an ally for increased attack speed and healing.

Doctrine’s Infuse takes things to the next level by adding extra power to whichever ability he uses next, like gaining free-flight when infusing his Shrouded Momentum or piercing damage when infusing his next Eternal Scepter attack. Finally, unleash his Ultimate, Deliverance, to grant allies overhealth while reducing the maximum health of your enemies.
